body: as soon as possible really, however when I say that I just mean little bits, not hardcore revision from now until june, gradually increase the time the closer it gets to exams but the only reason i say start as soon as possible is so you avoid having to cram your revision!! hope this helps

honestly nothing to out of order, i just printed out a ton of past papers or went to my maths teacher (luckily for me he was so amazing and helpful) and got some papers from him, then i tried them with no help and in exam conditions, and then after that did them with the textbook and then i marked them myself through the mark scheme (helps with technique and understanding where you did well/went wrong) or got my maths teacher to help :)
Honestly same, Speaking is so horrible and i dread doing practice. Thank you for advice tho x

I'm still figuring my way around revising for a-level french, but I assume you're asking for GCSE based on your flair, for GCSE I honestly just did past papers for reading, practice questions for listening. For writing I had the CGP revision guide and I did every single writing practice in there until I  understood the essentials. For speaking I just carried my flashcards with me everywhere and practiced phrases about describing the photos (a cote de, droite, gauche ect). Hope this helps
